key_insight: The paper shows that the representation space in world-action models is crucial for learning good robot policies, and that neither perfect reconstruction nor generic pre-trained features are enough on their own. It introduces ReWAM, which uses calibrated DINO-based features to better align prediction with control.
problem_solved: World-action models need a shared latent space that supports both future prediction and action planning, but it is unclear what kind of representation best enables policy learning. This paper addresses how to design that space so it works effectively for robotics control.
method: Run controlled comparisons to test different representation choices for world-action modeling.
Find that reconstruction-heavy and pre-trained perceptual representations each have limitations for policy learning.
Propose ReWAM, a representation-centric model built on pre-trained DINO features with feature calibration and temporal representation alignment.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work shifts attention from only model scale or reconstruction quality to the design of the latent representation itself. It offers a practical direction for building better robot learning systems that are more effective for both prediction and control.
